cover.title: decoded.
cover.sub: Most products are made for one type, not all four.

slides.title: Oily
slides.body: Shine by midday, larger pores, breakouts. Look for lightweight gels, niacinamide, BHA.

slides.title: Dry
slides.body: Tight after washing, flaky patches, dull. Look for ceramides, hyaluronic acid, creams over gels.

slides.title: Combination
slides.body: Oily T-zone, dry cheeks. Look for balancing toners and light moisturisers.

slides.title: Sensitive
slides.body: Redness, stings easily. Look for fragrance-free formulas, centella, short ingredient lists.

end.title: Not sure which one you are?
end.sub: Kobi asks five questions and sets your profile once.

cover.title: 60 seconds.
cover.sub: Five steps, in this order. Everything else is optional.

slides.title: Cleanse
slides.body: Oil cleanser at night if you wore SPF or makeup, then a gentle foam.

slides.title: Tone
slides.body: Not the harsh kind. A hydrating toner that preps your skin.

slides.title: Treat
slides.body: One serum, one goal. Add a second only once the first works.

slides.title: Moisturise
slides.body: Gel for oily, cream for dry. Lock in what you just applied.

slides.title: Protect
slides.body: SPF50+ PA++++ every morning, even indoors.

end.title: Kobi builds the five for you.
end.sub: From your skin type and products you can find in Korea.

cover.title: Niacinamide.
cover.sub: Vitamin B3. The one almost everyone can use.

slides.title: What it does
slides.body: Evens out tone, calms redness, supports the barrier and helps keep oil in check.

slides.title: How much
slides.body: Most Korean serums use 2 to 5%. Higher isn't better: 10% and up can irritate.

slides.title: Pairs well with
slides.body: Hyaluronic acid, ceramides, centella and SPF. Fine with retinol too.

slides.title: Go slow if
slides.body: Your skin is very sensitive. Start every other day and watch for flushing.

end.title: Scan the bottle.
end.sub: Kobi shows what's inside and whether it fits your skin.

cover.title: Centella.
cover.sub: Cica, tiger grass, 병풀. Korea's favourite calming ingredient.

slides.title: What it does
slides.body: Soothes redness and irritation and supports the skin barrier.

slides.title: On the label
slides.body: Centella Asiatica Extract, Madecassoside, Asiaticoside. Any of these means cica.

slides.title: Best for
slides.body: Sensitive and acne-prone skin, after exfoliation, after sun.

slides.title: Pairs well with
slides.body: Niacinamide, hyaluronic acid, panthenol. Great in a toner or a light cream.

end.title: Reactive skin?
end.sub: Tell Kobi. It flags the products that calm, not sting.

cover.title: Korean label.
cover.sub: Five words that tell you what the product does.

slides.title: Moisturising
slides.body: Hydration. Toners, essences, gel creams.

slides.title: Soothing
slides.body: Calming. Usually centella, mugwort or heartleaf inside.

slides.title: Brightening
slides.body: Tone-evening. Niacinamide, vitamin C, arbutin.

slides.title: Wrinkle care
slides.body: Anti-ageing. Adenosine, peptides, retinol.

slides.title: Sun protection
slides.body: It's a sunscreen. Look for SPF50+ and PA++++.

end.title: Or just scan it.
end.sub: Kobi translates the whole ingredient list for you.

cover.title: done right.
cover.sub: How to shop the biggest K-beauty store without wasting money.

slides.title: Time it with a sale
slides.body: Olive Young runs big sale events several times a year. Check the app first.

slides.title: Use the testers
slides.body: Try the texture on your hand before you buy the full size.

slides.title: Bring your passport
slides.body: Visitors can get the tax back. Ask at the counter.

slides.title: Ignore the hype tag
slides.body: Bestseller means popular, not right for your skin.

slides.title: Mini first
slides.body: Most hits come in mini sizes. Try for two weeks, then go big.

end.title: Kobi works in the aisle.
end.sub: Scan, compare, decide. Then pay.

cover.title: decoded.
cover.sub: Why Korean sunscreens are the ones people fly home with.

slides.title: SPF50+
slides.body: Protection from UVB, the burning rays. 50+ is the norm in Korea.

slides.title: PA++++
slides.body: Protection from UVA, the ageing rays. Four plus signs is the top grade.

slides.title: Texture
slides.body: Light, no white cast, no greasy film. That's why people actually wear it.

slides.title: How much
slides.body: Two finger-lengths for the face. Reapply every two hours outdoors.

slides.title: Every day
slides.body: Cloudy, winter, by a window. UVA gets through.

end.title: Need one for your skin?
end.sub: Gel for oily, cream for dry, mineral for sensitive. Ask Kobi.

cover.title: vs night.
cover.sub: Same five steps. Different job.

slides.title: Morning protects
slides.body: Light cleanse, toner, vitamin C or niacinamide, light moisturiser, SPF.

slides.title: Night repairs
slides.body: Double cleanse, toner, your active, a richer cream. No SPF.

slides.title: Split your actives
slides.body: Retinol at night, vitamin C in the morning. Exfoliate two or three nights a week.

end.title: Kobi splits it AM / PM.
end.sub: And tells you which active goes where.

cover.title: that waste your haul.
cover.sub: And how to fix each one.

slides.title: Everything at once
slides.body: Add one new product at a time, two weeks apart.

slides.title: Over-exfoliating
slides.body: Two or three nights a week. Redness and tightness mean stop.

slides.title: Mixing actives
slides.body: Retinol plus acids plus vitamin C in one go damages the barrier.

slides.title: Skipping SPF
slides.body: Serums work for months. The sun undoes it in an afternoon.

slides.title: Copying someone else
slides.body: The viral serum was made for a skin type. Maybe not yours.

end.title: Scan before you buy.
end.sub: Kobi checks the product against your skin, not the hype.

slides.title: No tipping
slides.body: Not in restaurants, not in taxis. It isn't expected.

slides.title: Press the bell
slides.body: Restaurants have a call button on the table. Use it.

slides.title: Two hands
slides.body: Give and receive cards, cash and gifts with both hands.

slides.title: Shoes off
slides.body: At homes, many guesthouses, some restaurants. Look for the shoe shelf.

slides.title: Quiet on the metro
slides.body: Calls and loud talking are frowned upon.
